questions.html: What does the Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) represent for a continuous random variable?

options.html: The probability density at a specific point
The probability of the random variable taking a value less than or equal to a given value
The expected value of the random variable
The variance of the random variable

questions.solution:
(b)
The Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) of a continuous random variable at a particular point represents the probability that the random variable takes a value less than or equal to that point.

questions.tags: Technical • Data Science and artificial Intelligence • +1 / -0.33
questions.html: Which of the following statements about the Poisson distribution is true?

options.html: It is a continuous probability distribution.
It is used to model the number of successes in a fixed interval of time or space.
It has a single parameter, which represents the mean and variance of the distribution.
It is symmetric around its mean.

questions.solution:
(b)
The Poisson distribution is used to model the number of successes (events) that occur in a fixed interval of time or space.

questions.html: In a normal distribution, what percentage of the data lies within one standard deviation from the mean?
questions.solution:
68.27
In a normal distribution, approximately 68.27% of the data falls within one standard deviation from the mean according to the empirical rule (also known as the 68-95-99.7 rule).

questions.html: If X follows a uniform distribution over the interval [4, 10], what is the probability of X being exactly 7?
questions.solution:
(a)
In a continuous uniform distribution, the probability of obtaining an exact value is zero, as the distribution is continuous and uniform over an interval.
Therefore, the probability of X being exactly 7 in this case is 0.
